description: The bar chart, titled “Researcher Location,” displays the number of datasets published annually from 2012 to 2022, categorized by researcher location, with the horizontal axis labeled “Year” and the vertical axis labeled “Number of datasets” on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^2. The chart uses grouped bars for each year, with each group containing six bars representing: “Other” (blue), “UK” (red), “USA” (orange), “IT” (purple), “IN” (green), and “DE” (brown), as indicated by the legend. The USA consistently produced the highest number of datasets each year, with values peaking at 50 in 2020 and again at 50 in 2021. In 2021, India (green) surpassed the UK (red), with 30 datasets compared to 20. Germany (brown) showed a steady decline after 2018, dropping from 10 in 2018 to 10 in 2019, then to 5 in 2020, and finally to 1 in 2022. The “Other” category (blue) was the second most frequent contributor, with values ranging from 1 in 2012 to 50 in 2021. The “IT” (purple) and “UK” (red) categories generally remained low, with “IT” reaching 10 in 2019 and 2020, and “UK” reaching 20 in 2021. The bars are not sorted, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and height.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of datasets over time for the five most frequent researcher locations and all other locations combined, spanning the years 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the years, while the vertical axis indicates the number of datasets on an exponential scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^2. Researchers from the USA consistently published the highest number of datasets across all years, with a peak in 2020. Notably, researchers from India surpassed those from the UK in dataset production in 2021, marking a significant shift in contributions. Additionally, the number of datasets from Germany declined steadily after 2018, indicating reduced activity in dataset production from this region.
